statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 59 registered checks and four representative public templates. Search results, authenticated account flows, live playback internals and every regional section were not covered because they either repeat audited templates or cross into separate/authenticated surfaces.

paths.description: Homepage and primary news discovery feed; represents the entry template, global navigation, consent UI and main content discovery.
Lead economy article; represents the core reading journey and article/detail template.
Latest-news listing; represents section/index feeds and chronological discovery.
Video listing; represents media-heavy discovery and video content.

findings.summary: No user-preference-driven dark theme
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical to the light screenshot and the platform probe reports computed colorScheme "normal".
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide prefers-color-scheme/light-dark() surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: Animations remain active with reduced motion requested
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe confirms the media query is active but still finds three 1,000 ms document animations, including running animations.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove non-essential animation or reduce it to a near-instant, non-spatial transition.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: The platform probe reports no View Transition support usage while the site exposes hundreds of navigational links and interactive menu/search states.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route and major state changes with same/cross-document View Transitions, retaining instant navigation as fallback.

findings.summary: Consent prompt obscures primary content on every entry template
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots of the homepage, article, latest-news and videos templates show a large fixed consent prompt covering the lower content, with only a prominent “Prosseguir” action.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, accessible consent surface that does not cover core content and offers clear accept, reject and preference actions.

findings.summary: Overlay UI is not built from semantic top-layer primitives
findings.evidence: The DOM/platform probe finds 0 dialog, 0 popover and 0 details elements despite rendered consent, menu, account and search overlay controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal consent and popover/details for transient menu/disclosure UI, with native focus and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Advertising and consent chrome dominate the first viewport
findings.evidence: Homepage and listing screenshots devote most of the initial viewport to an empty/ad slot plus the consent panel, leaving little editorial content visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve smaller ad slots, collapse unfilled inventory promptly, and keep consent chrome outside the main reading area.

findings.summary: Article template overflows by 634 CSS pixels on mobile
findings.evidence: At 360x800, the article layout primitive reports scrollWidth 994, clientWidth 360 and horizontalOverflowPx 634; the probe identifies the off-canvas account drawer and quote carousel extending to 1,988 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Constrain off-canvas drawers to the visual viewport, clip their containing layer, and make the quote carousel intrinsically size within 100% inline-size.

findings.summary: Reused components do not use component-level responsive rules
findings.evidence: The platform probe finds zero container-query rules; the article quote carousel and drawer overflow while reused global components depend on viewport layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, ticker/carousel and drawer shells containment and size-aware @container adaptations, with intrinsic fallbacks.

findings.summary: Some focusable controls have tiny targets or no visible focus
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe measures the Menu button at 12x2 CSS px and finds several later controls with outline none; some could not receive focus when programmatically focused.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the actual interactive box at least 44x44 CSS px and provide a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator on every control.

findings.summary: Homepage load is slow and interaction readiness is poor
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports performance 0.38, LCP 6.4 s, TBT 1,020 ms and TTI 52.6 s; the independent trace reports LCP 5.89 s and TBT 984 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset/content, delay non-critical advertising/analytics, and break up startup work until LCP and interaction metrics are in the good range.

findings.summary: Load-time layout shift is just outside the good range
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports CLS 0.106 and identifies CLS culprits; 8 of 10 homepage images and 18 of 20 article images lack explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image, ad and late-content space with width/height or aspect-ratio and use stable font fallbacks.

findings.summary: Heavy scripts block the main thread
findings.evidence: The trace records 7 long tasks, a 574 ms longest task and 984 ms total blocking; Lighthouse attributes 8.7 s of main-thread work and 4.8 s script bootup.
findings.suggestedFix: Split and schedule startup tasks, move eligible computation off-thread, and defer ad/player/measurement code until needed.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is overwhelmed by a large dependency graph
findings.evidence: The HAR records 250 requests and 6.21 MB transferred, including parser-inserted critical CSS, many scripts and multiple redirects; 244 requests and 6.06 MB are classified off the main origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical chains, preload only true LCP dependencies, defer non-critical scripts and apply useful cache/compression headers.

findings.summary: Several megabytes of JavaScript are unused during load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 2,637 KiB unused JavaScript; the 1.2 MB player bundle alone has about 1.04 MB unused on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load the player and advertising integrations only when their UI is near use, and remove duplicate/legacy bundles.

findings.summary: Some links have no discernible name or mismatched accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility finds unnamed image links and visible-label/accessible-name mismatches for network brand links.
findings.suggestedFix: Give linked images meaningful alt/aria-label text and ensure each accessible name contains its visible label.

findings.summary: Heading and focus semantics contain gaps
findings.evidence: The homepage platform probe finds an empty H1; Lighthouse finds malformed list content, and the focus probe finds visible controls that reject focus or suppress outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a meaningful H1, valid list children, and a logical, consistently visible keyboard focus order.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow and target sizing are not consistently usable
findings.evidence: The article has 634 px horizontal overflow at 360 px and the Menu target is measured at 12x2 px, preventing reliable reflow and touch operation.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix inline overflow at narrow widths and enlarge interactive hit areas without disabling user scaling.

findings.summary: The homepage emits runtime and network errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records Bastian Failed to fetch errors, CORS failures and advertising API errors in the console.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle expected network failures without console errors and correct or remove failing cross-origin integrations.

findings.summary: Image markup omits intrinsic dimensions and often usable alternatives
findings.evidence: The image primitive finds dimensions missing on 8/10 homepage and 18/20 article images; it also reports 10/10 homepage image elements without alt, including linked editorial thumbnails.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height for every content image and purposeful alt text for linked editorial imagery; use empty alt only for truly decorative images.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and platform lifecycle blockers remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports two deprecated API warnings, inspector issues and an unload handler in a subframe that prevents BFCache restoration.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or isolate deprecated ad dependencies, remove unload handlers, and resolve DevTools inspector issues.

findings.summary: Some navigation links are not crawlable
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies three footer/menu anchors using href="javascript:void(0)" and several unnamed links, despite most content links being real URLs.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions and real destination href values for navigation, with descriptive link text.

findings.summary: Transport policy and cookie hardening are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers show HTTPS and nosniff but no HSTS; CSP is only upgrade-insecure-requests. The cookie audit finds numerous analytics identifiers without Secure and widespread SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, a restrictive nonce/hash-based CSP, and set Secure plus the narrowest suitable SameSite policy on all cookies.

findings.summary: The page activates an exceptionally broad tracking footprint
findings.evidence: The tracker primitive observes 85 third-party origins and 25 known tracker hosts; the HAR attributes 244/250 requests and 6.06/6.21 MB to origins outside g1.globo.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors, gate non-essential analytics/advertising on explicit consent, batch events and enforce strict retention/data-minimisation contracts.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive finds no HSTS, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; the CSP has no source restrictions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, frame-ancestors, strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, then harden CSP sources and Trusted Types where applicable.

findings.summary: Consent presents continuation without an equivalent refusal choice
findings.evidence: Across templates the consent panel explains personalization and advertising but exposes only the primary “Prosseguir” button; trackers and cookies are already present in fresh sessions.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent accept, reject and manage choices before non-essential storage or tracking starts, and make later withdrawal easy.

findings.summary: Search input disables browser autocomplete
findings.evidence: The article metadata/form probe finds the named, labelled search field with autocomplete="off".
findings.suggestedFix: Allow appropriate search autocomplete/history behavior unless there is a documented privacy reason to suppress it.

findings.summary: Image delivery still relies heavily on legacy formats and incomplete responsive markup
findings.evidence: Homepage inspection finds 6 legacy-format images and only 1 modern-format image; article inspection finds 7 legacy and 0 modern, with 14 images lacking srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Negotiate AVIF/WebP, provide srcset/sizes, and retain intrinsic dimensions for every responsive image.

findings.summary: Large background advertising and measurement work runs on initial load
findings.evidence: The homepage issues 250 requests, loads an offscreen 1.2 MB player and about 800 KB Permutive script, and executes 83 scripts before any video interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer player, ad auctions and measurement until visible/consented, coalesce analytics, and stop background work when hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes nearly the entire page budget
findings.evidence: HAR evidence attributes 6.06 MB of 6.21 MB and 244 of 250 requests to non-main origins, disproportionate for a text-led news homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template third-party budgets, remove low-value vendors, lazy-load media code and cache reusable assets.

findings.summary: Initial memory footprint is disproportionate for a news homepage
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary reports 1,523,846 heap nodes and 91.6 MB self size before meaningful interaction. Repeated scrolling did not increase it, but the starting footprint is high.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load large integrations, release unused caches/observers and profile the dominant constructors with a dedicated heap analyzer.
